messages:
alex: Customer AcadiaHealth (private deployment) reporting sudden 502s to /v1/generate since 07:22 UTC after their DX failover. Support ticket SUP-4982. Customer says IPsec fallback to VPN happened. Need triage.
maya: Do we have any customer logs or pcap? 502s + TLS errors could be multiple things.
alex: Customer logs show repeated TLS handshake errors: 'tls: handshake failure' and upstream 502 from our private LB. They also included a small tcpdump showing retransmits and ICMP type3 code4 (frag needed). Attaching snippet they pasted.
incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0423 for SUP-4982 (auto-created on escalation).
neteng: Quick checklist: verify UDP/4500 allowed (NAT-T), check ipsec rekey logs, and confirm BGP routes after failover. IPsec rekey under NAT can change ports and break state.
sre-oncall: Ask them to run these and paste output: ``ipsec statusall``, ``sudo tcpdump -n -i <edge> port 4500 or port 500 or icmp``, ``traceroute -n <private-lb-ip>``, and ``openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.private -tlsextdebug``.
alex: Customer tcpdump snippet:
```
09:22:13.123456 IP 10.0.0.5.443 > 192.0.2.10.52344: Flags [P.], seq 1:1401, ack 1, win 29200, length 1400
09:22:13.123457 IP 192.0.2.10 > 10.0.0.5: ICMP 3/4 Destination unreachable - Fragmentation needed and DF set
09:22:13.223500 Retransmission, packet lost
```
maya: That 1400 payload + ICMP frag needed + DF set = PMTU/MSS blackhole. When IPsec encapsulation adds headers, packets exceed path MTU. Common after DX->IPsec failover if path changes (extra encapsulation) or BGP hairpin causes transit.
neteng: Also check BGP: if routes were withdrawn and re-advertised, traffic might be hairpinned via transit with extra encapsulation, pushing packet size over MTU. I see BGP flap for peer AS 65012 at 07:21 in the peering logs.
alex: Customer also reported DNS briefly resolving to an older HA VIP in their peering VRF right after failover; could be stale route -> hairpin.
sre-oncall: Immediate mitigations:
1) Ask customer to ensure UDP/4500 and ESP allowed on their firewall (NAT-T + IPsec).
2) Apply MSS clamping on the customer edge or our private LB: iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
3) As a short-term we can reduce MTU on our private interface (e.g., to 1400) to avoid fragmentation.
neteng: I'll open NET-6721 to track BGP session resets and route advertisement changes during the failover window.
support-bot: SUP-4982 updated: escalated to NetEng (NET-6721) and SRE; customer informed of suggested workarounds.
maya: Additional repro steps for customer if we need pcap: run ``sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/acadia.pcap host <private-lb-ip>`` and share via secure upload. Also run ``sudo iptables -t mangle -S | grep TCPMSS`` to show existing clamps.
sre-oncall: Plan: I'll push a temporary TCPMSS clamp on the private LB and monitor for 30m. If that reduces 502 rate, we roll the change to other private edges. ETA ~20m.
alex: Updating customer with the plan and asking for tcpdump + ipsec logs. Also told them to confirm UDP/4500 open.
neteng: Confirmed BGP withdraw/advertise sequence caused next-hop change and likely hairpin path adding ~60 bytes of overhead. NET-6721 created with full logs.
alex: Customer reports partial improvement after we applied MSS clamp: 502s dropped by ~80% and TLS handshakes succeeding more often. They're continuing to run load tests. Will keep SUP-4982 open until fully stable. :thumbsup:
summary: Private deployment 502s after DX failover; chain: BGP flap -> route hairpin -> extra encapsulation -> PMTU blackhole -> TLS handshake failures. Mitigation: MSS clamping on LB/customer edge, ensure UDP/4500+ESP allowed, neteng tracking BGP issue.
